title: Governed information domains have explicit tool authority
test_intent: Determine whether each governed information domain in scope has an explicit authoritative tool or environment assignment with declared lifecycle context, governing references and change authority, rather than relying on implied authority from workflow or tool usage.

applicability.applies_when: A governed information domain is created, edited, hosted, transformed or exchanged through one or more tools or environments.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No governed information domain or tool/environment authority decision is in scope.

required_evidence: declared authoritative environment and non-authoritative environments
approved project deviation where organization-level authority is specialized

result_logic.pass: Every applicable governed information domain resolves to one explicit authoritative environment for the stated scope and lifecycle context, with no conflicting authority assignment.
result_logic.fail: An applicable governed information domain has no explicit authoritative environment, has conflicting authoritative environments for the same scope/context, or relies only on implied authority from workflow, convenience or technical capability.
result_logic.not_applicable: No governed information-domain tool-authority decision applies to the tested scope.
result_logic.indeterminate: The domain boundary, lifecycle context, registry entry, or approved project deviation is unavailable or insufficient to establish authority.

provenance.migration_note: Promotes the source validation hook into abstract conformance without inventing any product-specific authority assignment. Empty or incomplete registry coverage remains visible rather than being silently normalized.
